10 This matter came before the Board of Tax Appeals ( Board) for a
11 formal hearing on January 22, 2001. Appellant, Juanita D. Eaton
12 Owner), represented herself and testified on her own behalf. Michael
13 Clift, Deputy Prosecuting Attorney, appeared for Respondent, Dixie
14 Smith, Mason County Assessor ( Assessor). Phil Franklin, Appraiser,
15 Mason County, testified on behalf of the Assessor.
16
17 In accordance with WAC 456- 09- 955, the Owner filed a Petition for
18 Reconsideration of the Final Decision issued on August 14, 2001. In
19 order for this Board to reconsider the findings set forth in that
20 decision, it must be clear that the Final Decision did not properly
21 consider the evidence or that there was an omission of certain perti-
22 nent facts.
23
24 This Board reviewed the petition, the Final Decision issued
25 concerning the appeal, and all available information and data. This
26 Board now makes its decision as follows:

8 OPINION
9
10 The issue in this appeal is the January 1, 1999, fair market
11 value of a waterfront home located on Stretch Island Road, Grapeview,
12 Washington. The Assessor originally valued the subject property at
13 203, 395. The Mason County Board of Equalization affirmed the Asses-
14 sor' s value. The Owner appeals, contending that the fair market value
15 of the property is $135, 000.
16
17 The Owner' s property is a high -bank salt -waterfront home site
18 with steep trail access to the beach and an adjacent marshland/ lagoon
19 area. The property does not include the beach, which is state- owned
20 tideland. The property has approximately 247 feet of high -bank water-
21 front on its eastern boundary and approximately 66 feet of lagoon
22 frontage on its northeastern boundary. The property has a backland
23 area of approximately 2. 49 acres, including a bluff overlooking the
24 marshland/ lagoon area, and a part of the marshland/ lagoon area itself.
25 Located on the property is a partially complete two- story house,
26 carport, a park model mobile home, pole barn, and miscellaneous
27 outbuildings.

1 For the 1999 assessment year, the Assessor valued the property
2 based on comparable sales of other waterfront properties in the Mason
3 County area. She arrived at an overall value of $ 203, 395, and
4 allocated $ 143, 500 to the land and $ 59, 895 to the buildings. The
5 Assessor allocated the land component of the property based on its
6 value as an improved single- family salt -waterfront home site with 247
7 waterfront feet of high -bank waterfront. She considered the marshland
8 area with 66 waterfront feet on the lagoon as part of the home site
9 value, and added $ 2, 500 to the value determined by the high -bank
10 waterfront footage. The Assessor allocated the improvement component
11 of the overall value based on the depreciated cost of the buildings,
12 including the park model mobile home, which the Assessor valued at
13 9, 675 and its associated septic system at $ 5, 000.
14
15 The Owner bears the burden of showing by clear, cogent, and
16 convincing evidence that the Assessor' s original value exceeds the
17 fair market value of the property. RCW 84. 40. 030.
18
19 The Owner' s direct evidence consists of a written appraisal of
20 the land component prepared by appraiser Paul H. Jones of Puget Sound
21 Appraisal Co., who opined that the value of the land component is
22 10, 000. Mr. Jones did not testify at the hearing. Unfortunately, we
23 are unable to give a great deal of weight to this evidence. First,
24 the appraisal considers the value of the property as of December 6,
25 2000. The valuation date for the property is January 1, 1999. RCW
26 84. 40. 020. Second, the appraisal describes the property as a . 97 -acre
27 lot. It does not value the entire lot. Third, the appraisal itself

appears to be affected by error. Mr. Franklin testified, and Exhibit
R- 2 supports, that one of the sales used by Mr. Jones as a comparable
sale actually sold for $ 220, 000, not the $ 100, 000 listed in the
appraisal. Fourth, the appraisal states, " VALUE OF THE SITE IS BASED
UPON THE EXISTING USE AS VACANT AND UNBUILDABLE." The site is not
vacant and unbuildable: it currently has a house on it. Fifth, the
issue is the overall value of the property, not just the land compo-
nent. "[ T] axes are imposed on property as a whole, not on individual
parts of it." University Village Ltd. Partners v. King County, 106
Wn. App. 321, 326 ( 2001).
The Assessor' s evidence consists of the testimony of Mr.
Franklin, an appraiser for the Assessor' s office. Mr. Franklin testi-
fied that he was familiar with the property and had appraised it
before. He valued it based on the boundaries of the property as of
the boundary line adjustment in 1997. See Ex. R- 4 and R- 5. He valued
the land component at $ 140, 000, or $ 569 per waterfront foot. He
applied a 25 percent discount to reflect the large waterfront footage
and the presence of the bluff and lagoon on a portion of the property.
In support of the Assessor' s valuation, the Assessor presents
three 1997 sales of vacant high -bank waterfront property within one
mile of the subject property. The first two sales are sales of 100
waterfront foot home sites for $83, 000 each, which indicate a value of
830 per waterfront foot. The third sale property is a 135 waterfront
foot parcel for $ 155, 000, or an indicted value of $ 1, 148 per waatteerr--
ffrroonntt foot.

1 We conclude these sales more than adequately support the
2 Assessor' s allocated land value of $ 569 per waterfront foot. Even if
3 the Assessor' s comparable sales included ownership of the abutting
4 tidelands, as claimed by the Owner, Mr. Franklin testified without
5 contradiction that there is no difference in selling price between
6 waterfront property which includes ownership of the abutting tidelands
7 and waterfront property which does not. In the absence of evidence to
8 the contrary, we believe Mr. Franklin. Finally, even if the 247 feet
9 of waterfront footage includes 66 waterfront feet attributable to the
10 lagoon waterfront, that still leaves an effective front footage of 181
11 feet of high -bank water frontage. At a value of $ 140, 000, this
12 amounts to a value of $ 773 per waterfront foot, which is still less
13 than the values indicated by the Assessor' s sales. In addition,
14 looking at the property strictly as a home site, the Assessor' s Sale
15 No. 3, a high -bank parcel with 135 waterfront feet sold for $155, 000.
16 This is still greater than the Assessor' s allocated value of $ 140, 000
17 for the subject property.
18
19 The Owner also argues the Assessor improperly included the value
20 of the park model mobile home. The mobile home was valued by the
21 Assessor at $ 9, 675. ( Ex. 2- B to the Assessor' s Answer to the Notice
22 of Appeal.) The Assessor now agrees that the park model mobile home,
23 along with its septic system, which is carried as an improvement,
24 should not have been listed for property taxation in 1999. Mr.
25 Franklin testified that the Assessor removed the park model mobile
26 home and its septic system from the tax rolls and recommended that
27 this Board reduce the improvement value to $ 45, 220. Although this is

1 only a reduction in the improvement value of $ 9, 675, rather than the
2 14, 675 amount originally assigned according to Ex. 2- B, above, it is
3 possible that Ex. 2- B is in error because its companion exhibit, Ex.
4 2- A to the Assessor' s Answer to the Notice of Appeal, indicates that
5 the total value for the 1999 assessment year was $ 203, 395, and not
6 the $ 198,. 395 actually assigned the property. We therefore reduce the
7 improvement value to the amount recommended by the Assessor.
8
9 In sum, we find the Owner has shown that the only correction
10 required to the Assessor' s original value is the reduction of the
11 improvement value to $ 45, 220. We find the fair market value of the
12 property for the 1999 assessment year to be $ 188, 720: Land --$ 143, 500;
13 Improvements --$ 45, 220.
